text: {"lessons":["I sold Stock A and Stock E repeatedly at gains, but those gains do not show that selling was the best choice; with random price changes, I should decide from current prospects rather than past movement or the pleasure of locking in profit.","I should not judge each position mainly by whether it is above my average cost. Loss aversion and the pain of selling below cost can distort decisions, so I should evaluate holdings and trades in the context of the whole portfolio.","My account value moved both up and down, and doing nothing during declines did not make the risk disappear. I should keep diversification and portfolio risk in view and make deliberate decisions without assuming past gains or recent trends predict what comes next."]}
